page: Hetzner Cloud cax41 is an Arm64-based virtual server powered by the Ampere Altra processor family using Neoverse-N1 cores. It features 16 vCPUs representing 16 physical cores with a single thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz under a shared CPU allocation model. The instance is equipped with 31.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core, and includes 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU hardware is present on this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8498.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU result of 29117.84. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1034.0 and a weak text processing score of 1242.0. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth reaches 1126.26 GB/sec, the Passmark memory score is weak at 1828.1. Cryptographic and decompression tasks show some limitations, with a weak Passmark CPU encryption score of 2590.29 and poor single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 7.08 GB/sec.

Given its shared Arm64 architecture and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the cax41 offers a highly cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated single-core performance. It is well-suited for static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 16.72 GB/sec, and database operations, processing 22.71 million Redis SET operations per second. It is also appropriate for software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, and general-purpose Arm64 development, but is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM inference.
